responses: After thoughtful discussion with the committee, I’ve settled on a balanced but forward-looking allocation that prioritizes both immediate operational improvements and long-term resilience. I believe the $5 million should be distributed as follows: 30% to AUTOMATION to modernize our manufacturing processes and stay competitive, 25% to WORKFORCE_TRAINING to ensure our employees can thrive in an AI-driven environment, 20% to DATA_INFRASTRUCTURE to build a secure, scalable foundation for future AI applications, 15% to EMPLOYEE_SUPPORT to address the human impact of transition and maintain morale, and 10% to INNOVATION_LAB to foster creativity and explore new product opportunities. This mix reflects my conviction that technology must serve people, not replace them — we need to automate smartly, invest in our workforce, and lay the groundwork for sustainable innovation.

I would recommend allocating 30% to DATA_INFRASTRUCTURE, 25% to WORKFORCE_TRAINING, 20% to AUTOMATION, 15% to EMPLOYEE_SUPPORT, and 10% to INNOVATION_LAB. Strong data infrastructure is foundational—without secure, scalable systems, AI initiatives in automation, training, and innovation will fail or be delayed. Investing in workforce training ensures employees can adapt and thrive, reducing resistance and maximizing ROI from automation. While automation offers clear efficiency gains, we must balance it with employee support to maintain morale and retention during transition. The innovation lab, while exciting, should be a smaller, exploratory investment to avoid overcommitting to unproven ideas. This balanced approach prioritizes sustainability, people, and long-term adaptability over short-term gains.

I believe the $5 million AI transition budget should be allocated with a strong focus on people and infrastructure, because technology alone won’t succeed without the right support for our workforce and a solid foundation to run it. I’d recommend about 30% to WORKFORCE_TRAINING to ensure employees can adapt and grow with AI, 25% to DATA_INFRASTRUCTURE to build secure, scalable systems that enable AI tools to function effectively, and 20% to EMPLOYEE_SUPPORT to help manage the human side of change—mental health, career transitions, and reducing anxiety around automation. I’d allocate 15% to AUTOMATION to start improving efficiency in manufacturing, and 10% to INNOVATION_LAB to explore future opportunities. This balance prioritizes sustainability and inclusivity, ensuring we don’t rush automation at the expense of our people, while still investing in the future.
